products.name: Unified Agent Runtime
products.description: The canonical runtime for Rootz AI agents. Provides AgentEvent type system (25 categories), InternalChain (Merkle-linked blocks), SkillRegistry (manifest validation), and Zod schemas for runtime validation. TEE is the container. Skills are loaded code. Secrets are state.

products.name: Agent Wallet SDK
products.description: External developer SDK for AI agents with provable origin. Three calls: createAgentWallet() → recordInference() → settle(). Provider-agnostic — works with any AI API. Includes checkpoint/resume with anti-replay.

products.name: Morpheus Agent (Skill #1)
products.description: Morpheus decentralized inference integration. Runs as standalone MCP server (6 tools) or as a skill loaded into the TEE runtime. Birth certificates, signed action chains, session archiving, secure channel.

products.name: Secure Channel
products.description: Three-layer signed communication between AI agents and inference providers. Layer 1: agent signs prompts (working). Layer 2: provider signs responses (patch ready). Layer 3: ECDH encrypted channel bound to hardware attestation — NVIDIA GPU Entity Attestation Token via NRAS, AMD SEV-SNP, OCI instance principal, or TPM quote (designed).

products.name: Hardware Attestation Binding
products.description: Binds an AI workload to the silicon that ran it. Platform attestation proves the plant, not the product: it establishes a genuine GPU with known firmware in a correct security configuration, and by design says nothing about model weights, prompt, or output. Rootz places an application-layer evidence hash (model measurement, signed prompt, output digest) into the 32-byte attestation nonce the hardware signs over, so the same signature that proves the silicon also covers the specific result. Turns platform attestation into per-result provenance.

products.name: Rootz Desktop V6
products.description: Electron desktop application providing TPM-sealed wallet keys, Secret/Note management on Polygon, ECDH encryption, IPFS upload, credit management, and MCP server for AI tool integration. The agent's Hardware Security Module.

glossary.definition: A permanent on-chain record created when an AI agent is born, naming its two parents: the AI model that powers it and the human who authorized it.
Cryptographic evidence linking an AI output to a specific agent, model, and authorizer — signed, hash-linked, and blockchain-anchored.
An encrypted on-chain data wallet that serves as an AI agent's permanent identity and audit trail. Notes accumulate as the agent's chain of experience.
A Merkle root covering all actions in a session, written as a single on-chain Note. One transaction proves the integrity of the entire session.
A signed communication layer between agent and inference provider. Layer 1: agent signs. Layer 2: provider signs. Layer 3: ECDH encrypted.
Not storage — a messaging framework. Write to an address, all devices watching receive the update. Carries data, code, policy, instructions, and receipts.
Off-chain accumulation of signed actions with periodic on-chain settlement via Merkle root. Efficient: one transaction covers N operations.
Progressive trust model: Layer 1 (agent signs), Layer 2 (provider signs), Layer 3 (ECDH + attested hardware), Layer 4 (model provenance from signed sources).

A hardware-signed report proving what a machine is and what it is running — firmware, VBIOS, security configuration — signed by a device identity key fused at manufacture. It proves the plant, not the product: by design it says nothing about model weights, prompt, or output.

The signed token a verifier returns after checking hardware attestation evidence. NVIDIA's Remote Attestation Service (NRAS) issues one for GPU confidential computing after validating the device certificate chain, OCSP revocation status, and measurements against Reference Integrity Manifests.

The seam that turns platform attestation into per-result provenance. The attestation request carries a 32-byte nonce that the hardware signs over; Rootz places an application-layer evidence hash there — model measurement, signed prompt, output digest — so the signature proving the silicon also covers the specific inference result.

Proof strength stated as a level, never a boolean. L0 none. L1 attested transport. L2 attested silicon (GPU confidential computing attests the platform). L3 measured weights bound to a declared model identity. A weak claim is not a fake claim; depth is disclosed, not implied.
